title: Looking for the perfect task manager
body:
(Isn’t everybody?) I’ve tried at least a dozen of them, including the heavy hitters (Things 3, OmniFocus, TickTick, Todoist) and a bunch of the lesser-knowns like Tappsk. Tappsk lands solidly in the top half of the list. Of course, everybody’s needs and wants are different, so YMMV. Tappsk has a pleasing, clean interface, including (of course) dark mode. It syncs promptly between devices and with 🍎 Calendar. Like TickTick, it has a discrete goals section (which can be hidden if you’re not into that). It runs natively on iPad, iPhone, 🍎 Watch and Mac. Unlike many of the lesser knowns, Tappsk on 🍎 Watch is actually useful - not too tiny to read or cluttered with info I don’t need, just a decently sized checkbox so I can mark off to-do’s on the go without needing to pull out my phone. Of course, there’s always something missing - for me, the option to hide completed entries from the task logbook would be great. I find it useful to be able to quickly check and see if I’ve (for example) paid a particular bill, but it becomes all but useless when cluttered with daily noise like ‘feed the cat’, ‘go for a run’ and a dozen other daily repeating reminders. Also, completed reminders continue to show up on the Apple Watch, forcing you to go into the logbook and delete them there - a tedious one-at-a-time process. Still, a solid app. I’m using it every day and looking forward to see where the devs take this one.

** edit: in response to the devs comment - thank you, but I’m looking specifically for a way to easily exclude (or delete) items from the logbook. I know they can be deleted, but it’s a tedious one-at-a-time process - select, click delete, then acknowledge the “are you sure?” dialog. It’d be helpful if I could at least select multiple entries to delete wholesale. As for marking them ‘disabled’ under tasks - show completed - that hides them from the today view on iPhone and iPad, but does nothing to remove them on Apple Watch. They must first be deleted from the logbook, one by one. Please accept this as my heartfelt request to address these issues. Other than those things of note, I think this is a stellar app!

title: Love the simplicity
body:
I just started using Tappsk for 2 days, moving from my other todo list apps. Tappsk has a simple interface, neat looking, and has mainly four sections to group your tasks in — Today, Tomorrow, this week and later. 

I find this useful, as once you enlist your tasks and group them into the above sections, you can be focused on what is in line for today and this week. Once the day moves to tomorrow, all your unfinished today’s tasks move to tomorrow, and the above four sections will remain. Your completed tasks are logged separately. This way, you don’t tend to miss anything, if you are disciplined to keep organizing. Less stress, more productivity. Love it team Tappsk. Keep it up.

title: WOW!! This is a stunningly original, useful and beautiful todo app!
body:
I am so impressed with this app that it’s hard to know where to begin. First of all, it looks amazing, super clean and pleasant on the eye. This is crucial when you use an app every day. The set of features is nearly perfect. Enough power to manage your life, but so much that it sends you off the rails. You can’t help but stay focused on what needs to get done, whether you want to or not 😌

It is eminently usable. The learning curve is almost non existent. Everything is where it should be, and everything does what you expect it to do. This is an amazing achievement for an app that is trying to do so much.

This app is so innovative that the developer must be a creative genius. The habit ifeature looks like nothing I’ve ever seen before. Habits are treated completely differently than tasks, which is totally appropriate. Yet at the same time they are smoothly integrated and easy to set up. They are beautiful and appealing, which matters when you’re trying to maintain habits.

The calendar integration is surprisingly useful and well done. The way your appointments integrare with the to do‘s just feels good. 

The home screen is also organized in a completely original manner. You have slots for today, tomorrow, this week and later. That is so perfect that I can’t believe no one else is doing it.

Lastly, there is a quick way to make new to do‘s using voice input. It doesn’t seem like much, but when you try it you’ll be blown away but how nice and direct it feels. 

There are other little niceties throughout. Really an amazing achievement. Please give it a try!

title: So far, this To Do List is pretty perfect...
body:
I have not committed to any in-app purchase yet, but I think I am going to throw the switch. This one has simple categories and works the way I kept a list in a Levenger circa, but it has the convenience of being able to move things around. 

It has categories for Home, Work, Shopping, Routine and Ideas. (The Ideas are hidden, so they do not clutter up the list of things one must do.) And it divides things between Tasks and Habits. 

And they are presented to you on a Today, Tomorrow, This Week and Later Home Screen.

All color-coded and logically arranged.

The only very small downside I have found so far, is that I sometimes want to add a task I have already done and would like to keep notes associated with it. It will let me add it, but will not let me add a completion date in the past. Perfectly logical that it wouldn’t, but being able to change that to a past date would be handy. Few people I imagine want to do this.
